definitions.gloss: paper-thin difference; razor-thin margin; very slight gap
definitions.explanation: An extremely small difference between two things. Often used to describe the narrow gap between success and failure, genius and madness, or two closely matched competitors.

examples.japanese: {勝敗|しょうはい}は{紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ}だった。
examples.english: The difference between victory and defeat was paper-thin.

examples.japanese: {天才|てんさい}と{狂気|きょうき}は{紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ}だと{言|い}われる。
examples.english: They say the line between genius and madness is paper-thin.

examples.japanese: {合格|ごうかく}と{不合格|ふごうかく}は{紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ}で、あと{一点|いってん}{足|た}りなかった。
examples.english: The gap between passing and failing was razor-thin — I was just one point short.

notes:
Literally 'the difference of a single layer of paper,' this expression vividly captures how thin the margin can be between two outcomes. The underlying word {紙一重|かみひとえ} (paper-thin) is the core metaphor and can also be used on its own as a noun.

USAGE:
- Frequently appears in the pattern AとBは{紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ} (the difference between A and B is paper-thin)
- Classic pairings: {成功|せいこう}と{失敗|しっぱい} (success and failure), {天才|てんさい}と{狂気|きょうき} (genius and madness)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ}で{勝|か}つ: to win by a hair's breadth
- {紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ}で{負|ま}ける: to lose by a hair's breadth
- {紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ}で{助|たす}かる: to narrowly escape

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {僅差|きんさ}: narrow margin — a neutral, factual term without the vivid imagery
- {際|きわ}どい: close; narrow — describes the closeness of a margin in a more colloquial way
